subject: Processor vs Service Provider: telemetry sandbox, onshore fallback & proof
messages:
From: Evan Cho <evan@clearsight.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@clearsight.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify processing role + telemetry proof for DPA

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Two quick asks so our legal and security teams can close the DPA review: 

1) We need explicit language confirming Redwood will act as a service provider (processor) for telemetry derived from our requests — not a "sale" under CCPA/CPRA. Can you confirm the proposed redline will reflect that?

2) Our security team wants a short, testable proof that telemetry (prefix logs, token-level aggregates) can be kept in a US-only onshore environment and that any subprocessors involved will run in an ephemeral sandbox for evaluation before onboarding.

If you can send a short playbook or matrix showing the processing boundary and an example sandbox spec, we can get legal to sign off faster.

Appreciate it — Evan
Security Architect
ClearSight Analytics

P.S. We prefer attachments (not inline) for any technical specs.

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan@clearsight.ai>
Cc: security@clearsight.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify processing role + telemetry proof for DPA

Evan — thanks, clear asks. Short answers up front: we can be contractually a service provider (processor) for the telemetry types you outlined, and we can provide an onshore-only execution path and an ephemeral subprocessor sandbox for your testing. Attached: processing-boundary-matrix.xlsx and telemetry-sandbox-spec.md. Also attaching dpa-redline-v2.pdf with the proposed language.

High level:
- Processor commitment: We will add a definition in the addendum stating Redwood "processes Customer Data as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA" and we will not engage in any activity considered a "sale" of personal data. Redline highlights on page 2.
- Onshore fallback: We operate a US-only telemetry lane (us-central) with enforced routing. If a regional failure occurs we fail open to a compatible US fallback for the metric pipeline; we will include an SLA exception in the addendum for cross-region fallback and provide monitoring hooks.
- Subprocessor sandbox: For ClearSight's security review we will provision an ephemeral sandbox environment that contains synthetic traffic for telemetry ingestion and processing. The sandbox will:
  * Be isolated VPC with temporary credentials
  * Run only in US regions (us-east/us-central)
  * Have limited retention (30 days) and audit logging exposed to you
  * Allow you to run your verification suite against a read-only telemetry export

Next steps:
1) Please review the attachments — processing-boundary-matrix.xlsx maps each telemetry artifact to a classification and execution zone.
2) If the matrix looks good, we can spin up the sandbox environment (ETA 3 business days) and provide a signed statement of onshore routing and encryption at rest (AES-256) for the sandbox data.

I'll loop in legal internally to confirm the exact clause language.

Best,
Priyom Das
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: processing-boundary-matrix.xlsx, telemetry-sandbox-spec.md, dpa-redline-v2.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarify processing role + telemetry proof for DPA — redline notes

Team — forwarding Evan's note and Priyom's proposed attachments. Quick legal notes from my review of dpa-redline-v2.pdf: 
- Need to add a short clause that expressly prevents any repurposing of telemetry for advertising or selling. Use: "Redwood will not sell Customer Personal Data or use Customer Personal Data for targeted advertising."
- Add explicit encryption proof language: include KMS key id placeholder and a line about rotation and customer auditability.
- For subprocessors: add a conditional onboarding clause — Redwood will provide 10 business days' notice and a 3rd-party security report (SOC or equivalent) before a subprocessor can begin handling telemetry in a non-sandbox environment. Sandbox onboarding may be faster (3 business days) with synthetic data only.

One other ask: Evan's team calls out "token-level aggregates." We should limit retention of raw token payloads to 7 days by default unless customer opts in for longer for debugging, and call out the retention in the processing matrix.

I'll mark up the redline and send a tracked-changes PDF by EOD. Priyom — can you confirm the proposed notices and the 3-day sandbox SLA?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan@clearsight.ai>, security@clearsight.ai
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify processing role + telemetry proof for DPA — consolidated next steps

Evan / ClearSight team — looping back with concrete next steps and an escalation path in case legal needs a faster turnaround.

Summary of commitments:
- Contract: Redwood to be designated as a service provider (processor) for telemetry in the addendum. No sale, no advertising use. Redline attached (see dpa-redline-v2.pdf).
- Onshore execution: Telemetry ingestion and processing for the ClearSight account will be pinned to US regions. We will provide a signed statement with KMS key id and AES-256 encryption details after sandbox provisioning.
- Subprocessor sandbox: We will provision an ephemeral sandbox (3 business day ETA). Sandbox spec attached (telemetry-sandbox-spec.md). Non-sandbox subprocessor onboarding will include a 10-business-day notice plus security evidence; sandbox-only tests can be completed in 3 business days with synthetic data.
- Retention: Default raw token retention 7 days; aggregated metrics retention per the attached matrix. Longer retention options can be added via explicit opt-in in the addendum.

Action items and links:
1) ClearSight: confirm acceptance of the processing-boundary-matrix.xlsx and the 7-day default retention. Reply to this thread to approve and we'll schedule sandbox provisioning.
2) Redwood Legal: final redline will be uploaded; Kimberly to send tracked changes by EOD.
3) Ops: On sandbox approval we will create a ticket and provide credentials and read-only export.

Contract signature: I'll open a DocuSign packet for the addendum once we have ClearSight approval on the matrix and retention. Link: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSign/Sign?token=abc123
Sales tracking: HubSpot: HS-4782 (contact link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/HS-4782)

Escalation path (if timeline slips):
- Day 3 after request: Priyom (privacy) escalation to Jonas Weber (Head of Customer Success)
- Day 5: Legal escalation to Kimberly Park
- Day 7: Exec escalation to Marissa Cole (VP Sales) for SLA exception request

Evan — if you confirm the matrix and retention, we'll provision sandbox and upload the signed onshore statement after setup.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: processing-boundary-matrix.xlsx, telemetry-sandbox-spec.md, dpa-redline-v2.pdf
